—Tonight, I cannot leave Sakura alone.

My presence may do nothing to help her. Even so, I want to remain at home, ready to run to her side at any moment.

“Do not misunderstand me. Sakura is not the only one in poor health. You are similarly exhausted, Shirou, and that is why we shall rest tonight.

The extra time will help you replenish your magical energy. You are not to push yourself.”

“Y-Your gratitude is unnecessary. I am your Servant, Shirou. Naturally, my lord’s health is my first concern.”

“And, Shirou? Is there no reward of some kind for so understanding a retainer?”

pages.en:
The daily practice I have recently neglected ends with astonishing ease.

Perhaps my contract with Saber provided the catalyst. Forming the Magic Circuits that once resisted me at every turn has now become simple.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I’ve skipped my daily routine for the past few days, but it went pretty smoothly tonight.
Even though it used to be a challenge, activating my Magic Circuit is easy now. Maybe it’s because of my contract with Saber.

If I am attacked without warning, having no means to counter at once will be fatal.

If I could at least halve the time—to thirty seconds or so—I might begin to see a way forward.

pages.jaRuby:
「そうですね。そうだといいです。
……それで、先輩はどうだったんですか？ わたし、先輩が子供の頃の話、あんまり聞いたことないんです」
pages.en:
“Yes. I hope so.

“…What about you, Shirou? I’ve barely heard anything about your childhood.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yes. I hope that’s true.
…So what about you, Senpai? I don’t hear much about when you were a child.”

pages.ja:
「え、俺……？ うーん、別に今と変わらないんじゃないかな。昼間は町じゅう走り回って、切嗣のメシを作って、夜はここでガラクタいじってた」
照れ隠しに頬を掻く。
……その、子供の頃とまったく変わっていないというのは、男としてどうかと思ったのだ。
pages.jaRuby:
「え、俺……？ うーん、別に今と変わらないんじゃないかな。昼間は町じゅう走り回って、[ruby text=オヤジ char=2]切嗣のメシを作って、夜はここでガラクタいじってた」
照れ隠しに頬を掻く。
……その、子供の頃とまったく変わっていないというのは、男としてどうかと思ったのだ。
pages.en:
“What, me…? Hmm. I don’t think I was much different from how I am now. I spent the days running all over town, cooked for Kiritsugu, and tinkered with junk in here at night.”

I scratch my cheek to conceal my embarrassment.

…As a man, I cannot help finding it troubling that I have not changed at all since childhood.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Uh, me…? Hmm, I don’t think I was too different. I was always running throughout the town during the daytime, making meals for my father, and messing around with stuff here at night.”
I get embarrassed, so I scratch my cheek.
…Does it mean I’m a failure as a man if I haven’t changed from when I was a kid?

pages.ja:
「うわ。町じゅうを走り回ってたんですか？」
「んー……その、パトロールの真似事。弱きを助け強きをくじくってのに、憧れてたんだ」
pages.jaRuby:
「うわ。町じゅうを走り回ってたんですか？」

pages.en:
“Oh. You ran all over town?”

“Hmm… It was a kind of make-believe patrol. I admired the idea of helping the weak and punishing the strong.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Wow. You were running throughout the town?”
“Yeah… I thought I was patrolling the town. I admired helping the weak and crushing the strong.”

pages.ja:
おもに戦場は公園だった。
あそこで同い年の連中と一緒に、わずかに年上の連中とケンカしたりするのは日常茶飯事だった気がする。
……いやまあ、中には同い年のクセに智謀に長けた、あくまのような強敵がいたよーないなかったよーな。

pages.en:
The park was my principal battlefield.

Fighting there beside children my own age against children a little older than us seems to have been an everyday occurrence.

…Though among them, there may or may not have been a demonic adversary my own age who possessed a terrifying gift for strategy.
pages.mirrorMoon:
My battlefield was mainly in the park.
I think it was an everyday thing to fight with children my age against people older than me.
…Hmm, now that I think about it, a smart and devil-like person was in my age group too…

pages.ja:
「なるほど、いじめっこから町を守ってたんですね。先輩、昔からそういう人だったんだ」
「桜。笑顔で言われると、さすがに我が身を振り返っちまうから止めてくれ。わりと恥ずかしい」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“I see. You were protecting the town from bullies. You’ve always been that kind of person, Shirou.”

“Sakura, please don’t say that with such a happy smile. It makes me look back upon myself, and frankly, it’s embarrassing.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I see, so you were protecting the town from bullies? You were like that even when you were little?”
“Sakura. Smiling like that reminds me of all the stupid things I did, so please stop. It’s pretty embarrassing.”

pages.ja:
「恥ずかしくなんかないです。わたし、子供のころに先輩と会ってたら、きっと子分にしてもらってました。
わたしみたいな引っ込み思案には、手を取って外に連れ出してくれる人がいないとダメなんです」
pages.jaRuby:
「恥ずかしくなんかないです。わたし、子供のころに先輩と会ってたら、きっと子分にしてもらってました。

“There’s nothing embarrassing about it. If I’d met you as a child, Shirou, I’m sure you would have made me your henchman.”

“Someone as withdrawn as I was needs another person to take her hand and lead her outside.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It’s not embarrassing at all. I would’ve been your sidekick if I met you as a child.
A shy person like me needs someone to drag her outside.”

pages.ja:
「……子分って、桜な」
……あ。いやまあ、たしかに子供の頃に桜がいたら、それこそ毎日特訓してたかも。
元気だせー、って、いっしょに川原を走ったり道場で正座したりしていた可能性が高い。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“…Your henchman, Sakura?”

…Ah. Still, if Sakura had been there during my childhood, I might very well have trained her every day.

I would probably have dragged her along the riverbank or made her sit formally in the dojo, all while telling her to cheer up.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…A sidekick?”
…Oh. Well, I might have trained Sakura every day if she’d been with me as a child.
I would’ve run by the river or sat in the dojo with her.

pages.ja:
つまり、それは傍から見ると子分そのものだ。
そして俺によって鍛えられた桜はたくましく成長し、
これとか、
これみたいに女の子の皮を被ったあくまになるのだ。

In other words, to any observer, she would have been my henchman in every respect.

And after being trained by me, Sakura would have grown strong and fearless,

becoming this,

or this—one more demon wearing the skin of a girl.

That’s pretty much what a sidekick would do.
Under my watchful eye, Sakura would become strong, and then she would turn into a devil like…
Her,
or her.

う」

Thank goodness. Truly, thank goodness Sakura remained gentle.

“…Okay. That’s fine, but, um… Can I ask you an awkward question?”
“…? Okay, what?”

pages.ja:

pages.mirrorMoon:

pages.jaRuby: 「……先輩は気にしてないんですか？ 知らない家に貰われて、いっぱいイヤなコトとかあったんじゃないんですか？」
pages.en: “…Doesn’t it trouble you? Being taken in by a family you didn’t know—weren’t there many painful things?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…Don’t you care about it? You were adopted into a stranger’s family, so, um… weren’t there a lot of things you didn’t like?”

pages.ja:
「あー、そりゃ藤ねえの入れ知恵だな。

“Ah, Fuji put that idea in your head.”

“…Well, perhaps the first year looked painful from outside. But it wasn’t so terrible in its own way, and I don’t remember anything I hated.”

“Th-Then were you happy, Shirou?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Oh, did Fuji-nee give you the wrong idea?
…Well, it might’ve looked that way when I first came here, but it wasn’t hard on me, and there was nothing I didn’t like.”
“Then was it fun for you, Senpai?”

pages.ja:
む。
楽しかったか、なんて訊かれたのは初めてだ。
あの火事の後。
切嗣との初めの一年間は、ただ傷が癒えるのに耐え続けた一年だったと思う。
pages.jaRuby:

あの火事の後。
切嗣との初めの一年間は、ただ傷が癒えるのに耐え続けた一年だったと思う。
pages.en:
—Hm.

No one has ever asked me whether I was happy.

After the fire,

the first year I spent with Kiritsugu was a year devoted solely to enduring the healing of my wounds.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Hm.
This is the first time I’ve been asked this question.
After that fire…
…My first year here was spent healing my wounds.

pages.ja:
……その後。
その後から今まで、ひたすら体を動かすだけの年月だった。
魔術を習うために切嗣を追い掛け続けて、
一人だけ助かった意味を探して、町じゅうを走り回った。
pages.jaRuby:

一人だけ助かった意味を探して、町じゅうを走り回った。
pages.en:
…And afterward.

From then until now, the years have been filled with ceaseless motion.

I followed Kiritsugu everywhere so he would teach me magecraft.

Searching for the meaning of being the only one who survived, I ran through every corner of the town.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…And after that…
My time until now has been spent in constant motion.
I studied magic to be more like Kiritsugu,
and I ran around the town, looking for the reason why only I survived that night.

pages.ja:
その日々が。
楽しかったかどうかなど、考える余裕がなかっただけだ。
pages.jaRuby:
その日々が。
楽しかったかどうかなど、考える余裕がなかっただけだ。
pages.en:
In all those days,

I simply never possessed the leisure to wonder whether I was happy.
pages.mirrorMoon: I never had time to wonder if I was enjoying myself.

pages.ja: 「うーん、どうだろう。楽しかったかどうかは分からない。ただ、俺は切嗣みたいになりたかった」
pages.jaRuby: 「うーん、どうだろう。楽しかったかどうかは分からない。ただ、俺は[ruby text=オヤジ char=2]切嗣みたいになりたかった」
pages.en: “Hmm. I don’t know whether I was happy. I only know that I wanted to become like Kiritsugu.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Hmm, I don’t know. I don’t know if it was fun for me or not. I just wanted to be like my father.”

恐る恐る桜は言う。

「
うん。おかしいかな」

Sakura asks timidly.

And I—

“—Yes. Does that sound strange?”

I scratch my cheek and answer with perfect honesty.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“You mean to be a superhero, like Fujimura-sensei said?”
Sakura asks timidly.
To that…
“Yeah. Is that weird?”
I answer while scratching my cheek.

“No. You aren’t mistaken, Shirou. You’re forthright, and admirable.”

“————”

Her calm words reach my heart so directly that instead of averting my eyes in embarrassment, as I ordinarily would, I want simply to thank her.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“No, I don’t think so. It’s amazing that you’re so sure of yourself.”
“”
Her words are calm.
I usually get embarrassed from such words, but her words hit me so much that I’m tempted to thank her.

pages.ja: 「じゃあもう一つ訊きますね先輩。もしわたしが悪い人になったら許せませんか？」
pages.jaRuby: 「じゃあもう一つ訊きますね先輩。もしわたしが悪い人になったら許せませんか？」
pages.en: “Then let me ask one more thing, Shirou. If I became a bad person, would you be unable to forgive me?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Here’s another question. Would you be able to forgive me if I become a bad person?”

「え……？」
唐突な質問に真っ白になる。
……ただ、それを本当に真剣に考えるのなら、
「ああ。桜が悪いコトをしたら怒る。きっと、他のヤツより何倍も怒ると思う」
俺は、何よりも優先して桜を叱り付けるだろう。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“What…?”

The sudden question empties my mind.

…But if I consider it with the seriousness it deserves—

“Yes. If you did something wrong, Sakura, I would be angry. I think I would be many times angrier with you than with anyone else.”

Before anything else, I would scold Sakura.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“What…?”
My head blanks out from the sudden question.
…But to answer seriously…
“No. I’d get mad if you do something bad. I’d get more mad than anybody else.”
I’d probably be first in line to scold her.

pages.ja:
「
良かった。先輩になら、いいです」
安心したように桜は頷く。
pages.jaRuby:
「
良かった。先輩になら、いいです」
安心したように桜は頷く。
pages.en:
“—Thank goodness. If it’s you, Shirou, I wouldn’t mind.”

Sakura nods in relief.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I’m glad. I’d want you to do that.”
Sakura nods in relief.

pages.ja:
「……？」
その笑顔を見て、以前にもこんなコトがあったような気がして首をかしげる。
pages.jaRuby:
「……？」

pages.en:
“…?”

Her smile leaves me with the sensation that something like this happened before, and I tilt my head.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…?”
Seeing her smile makes me think that something like this happened before.

pages.en:
“I’ll return to my room. Good night, Shirou.”

Sakura leaves.

Watching her retreat, I wonder why I cannot remember what the smile recalled.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I’m going back to my room. Good night, Senpai.”
Sakura leaves.
As I see her off, I try to remember where I’ve seen that smile before, but my memory fails me.

Taking care not to wake Saber, I slip beneath the covers. Just as I begin to close my eyes—

I return to my room.
I lie on my futon, trying not to wake Saber, and right when I’m about to close my eyes…

That was—yes—

Yes, it was

pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
It was the summer before last.

Sakura asked to begin helping at our house, and I refused her time after time.

Still, she would not surrender. With a stubbornness I could never have imagined from the Sakura I knew, she continued coming every day.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It happened during the summer two years ago.
I continued to refuse every time Sakura offered to come help me at my house.
But Sakura did not give up and kept visiting my house with obstinacy you would never expect from her.

土蔵に仕舞っておいた、切嗣が使っていた家の鍵を、そこで桜に手渡したのだ。
pages.en:
At last, I gave way—honestly, her earnest determination defeated me. In any case, I summoned her to the storehouse and declared my surrender.

“You win, Sakura. And because you win, you get this.”

An old key.

There, I gave Sakura the key to our house that Kiritsugu had once used and which I had kept in the storehouse.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I gave upwell, Sakura’s effort beat me to be exact, but I called Sakura to the shed and admitted my defeat.
“You beat me. I lost, so I’ll give you this.”
It was an old key.
I gave Sakura the key to my house that I kept in the shed which Kiritsugu used to use.

自分は他人だから合鍵なんてものは貰えない、なんてすっとんきょうなコトを言ったんだっけ。

Sakura was astonished. Embarrassed, she tried to refuse.

She said something absurd about being an outsider and therefore being unable to accept a duplicate key.

Surprised, Sakura tried to refuse.
She said something ridiculous about how a stranger couldn’t possibly accept such a gift.

これからは好きにうちを使ってくれ。……その、その方が、俺も助かる』

pages.en:
“Listen. You come here every day to help. How can you possibly be an outsider?

“From now on, use our house whenever you like. …It would make things easier for me too.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hey now. You’re coming to help me every day, so you’re no stranger.
Please feel free to use this. …Um, it would help me out if you did.”

幸せそうに頷いた、桜の顔を。

I said that and forced the key into her hands.

That was when I saw it.

“…Yes. Thank you, Shirou. This is the second time someone precious to me has given me something.”

Sakura’s face as she nodded in happiness.

I forced the key into her hands.
And that’s when I saw it.
“…Okay. Thank you, Senpai. This is the second gift I’ve received from someone dear to me.”
Sakura smiled happily as she nodded.

pages.en:
“Ah—of course.”

That was what had caught in my memory.

Sakura is earnest, and she always smiles gently.

But that was the only other time I had seen her smile with such perfect contentment—
